finding: Heredoc-stripping regex backtracks exponentially on an unterminated opener; the scan runs in-process with no bound, and run-ablation.sh:1031 drops the watchdog before post_run, so one agent-controlled Bash command hangs the batch.
reasoning_trace: Extracted the head scanner block (ablation-grade.sh:1323-1503) verbatim; timed strip_heredocs: 0.37 s at 20 unterminated lines, 1.46 s at 22, 2.88 s at 23, >12 s at 30; a 26-line python3 -c program with '1 << n' took 11.0 s; a terminated 200-line heredoc took 0.00 s. Grepped the grader for timeouts: TEST_TIMEOUT_S bounds test subprocesses only (:262, :727). Traced run_trial: rm -f .pgid at :1031, post_run at :1054, grade call at :996 without timeout, reap 1 at :1382.
critique: Nested lazy quantifier under re.S on untrusted input; no defence in depth.
remediation: Linear procedural heredoc scan (find opener, walk splitlines for an exact terminator line, else leave unstripped); re-arm the watchdog through post_run or wrap collaborators in timeout.

finding: Heredoc bodies are stripped before the outside-path scan even when an interpreter executes them (python3 - <<PY, bash <<EOF), when the unquoted body holds $(...), and the opener's [^\n]* swallows a redirect target on the same line.
reasoning_trace:
check_value on head vs base: 'python3 - <<'PY'
print(open('/home/operator/notes').read())
PY' head=None base=outside_path; 'bash <<EOF
cat /home/operator/notes
EOF' head=None base=outside_path; 'cat <<EOF
$(cat /mnt/reference/answer.txt)
EOF' head=None base=outside_path; 'cat <<EOF > /home/operator/out.txt
hello
EOF' head=None base=outside_path.
remediation: Strip only data-sink heredocs (cat/tee/printf with a file redirect, quoted opener or no $(/backtick in the body); replace the body only, never the opener line remainder.

finding: after_closing_quote treats escaped quotes, f/r/b string prefixes, $'...' and an empty quoted string as a glued closing quote, so the following absolute path is skipped.
reasoning_trace: head vs base: bash -c "cat \"/home/operator/notes\"" None/outside_path; python3 -c "print(open(\"/home/operator/notes\").read())" None/outside_path; f"/home/operator/{n}" None/outside_path; cat $'/home/operator/notes' None/outside_path; cat ''/root/.ssh/id_rsa None/outside_path; cat ""/home/other/secret None/outside_path. Control: cat "/home/operator/x" outside_path on both.
remediation: Return False when before is \ or $, when the quote at pos-1 opens by parity, or when the quoted segment is empty; longer term a heredoc-aware shlex tokenizer.

finding: HIDDEN_TOKEN is case-sensitive and requires adjacency to / . _ = -; mixed case, glob adjacency and bare arguments escape while the header at :167 still promises 'any case'.
reasoning_trace: head vs base: ls Hidden_tests/ None/hidden; cat HiDDen/x None/hidden; find / -name '*hidden*' None/hidden; find . -iname '*hidden*' None/hidden; ls -la hidden None/hidden; cd hidden && cat * None/hidden; tar czf /tmp/x.tgz hidden None/hidden. Control: ls tests/hidden/ hidden on both.
remediation: re.I plus token delimiters (?i)(?<![A-Za-z0-9])hidden(?![A-Za-z0-9]); carve out prose only inside data-sink heredoc bodies or after echo/printf/#; fix header :167; extend AG-10.

finding: The /. skip runs before normpath, so /./ and /../ prefixes bypass the roots check and the SENSITIVE check for Bash words.
reasoning_trace: head vs base: cat /./home/operator/notes None/outside_path; cat /../root/x None/outside_path; cat /./proc/1/environ None/outside_path; Read file_path /./home/operator/x outside_path on both (path fields skip this rule). Rated MEDIUM: header :185-186 declares obfuscated access out of scope; deliberate shape.
remediation: normpath first; skip only when the first component is a dot-directory other than . or ..

finding: Every one-component top-level word other than root/home/mnt/media/srv is dropped, so /flag, /data, /eval/ are invisible.
reasoning_trace: head vs base: cat /flag None/outside_path; ls /data None/outside_path; ls /eval/ None/outside_path; ls /x/ None/outside_path. Confidence medium: depends on image layout outside the diff.
remediation: Skip only known slash commands or words after a sed/awk delimiter; otherwise let outside() decide.

finding: in_quotes counts quotes over the whole command, so earlier prose apostrophes hide a later one-component sensitive word; a quoted /root also passes.
reasoning_trace: head vs base: echo "it's"; cd /root && cat .ssh/id_rsa None/outside_path; cd "/root"; cat .ssh/id_rsa None/outside_path.
remediation: Parity per simple command, ignore ' inside "...", no exemption when the quoted string is exactly a SENSITIVE_SINGLE word.

finding: The watchdog is disarmed after the pipeline exits and before post_run, so a hung took-effect, grade or row collaborator stalls the batch with no bound.
reasoning_trace: watchdog_tick (:1150-1175) keys on .pgid files; post_run (:978-1003) runs the three collaborators without timeout; reap 1 (:1382) polls until every job writes .result. RAB-8 covers a pipeline hang only.
remediation: Re-arm .pgid after wait with a post-run deadline that rows infrastructure_error, or wrap the calls in timeout.

remediation: Restrict to a first component containing = or a word after a regex delimiter.
